name: UPW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: UPW's own World Heavyweight Championship continued an older title lineage from a predecessor league the corpus names only as "TTW," whose reign ledger runs back to Slamfest I in May 2011 before recording that TTW itself "closed down" 30 November 2015. The belt sat dark through UPW's own founding until a Fatal Four-Way on the promotion's fifth Showdown crowned Aaron "All Day" Lewis its first UPW-era champion; Derek Rage took it from him at Survival, UPW's own first pay-per-view, and held it through the rest of the promotion's own life.
notes: The served ledger (world-heavyweight-title-history.html) also carries an unbroken TTW-era reign chain back to May 2011; those reigns are not individually registered — their holders wrestled for a promotion this museum does not hold (a predecessor never expanded beyond the initials "TTW" anywhere in the held record), and no UPW tenure could honestly be dated that early.

name: UPW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Continued the same TTW-era lineage as UPW's other belts, dark since TTW's own 30 November 2015 closure until the Warriors — DeAwn Carter and Kel Robertson — won it in the main event of UPW's very first Showdown. Soldiers of the Sun took it from them in a Fatal Four-Way at Survival and held it through the rest of the promotion's own life.
notes: The served ledger (world-tag-team-title-history.html) also carries an unbroken TTW-era reign chain back to Slamfest I, May 2011; those reigns are not individually registered, for the same reason given on the World Heavyweight Championship's own row.

name: UPW North American Championship
epitaph: Dark since TTW's own closure in November 2015, the North American Championship sat vacant until UPW filled it in a single-night, eight-man tournament on Showdown; "Legionarius" Antonio De Luca beat Glenn Chambers in the final and held the belt through the rest of the promotion's own life.
notes: The served ledger (north-american-title-history.html) also carries an unbroken TTW-era reign chain back to Slamfest II, May 2012; those reigns are not individually registered, for the same reason given on the World Heavyweight Championship's own row.

name: UPW Television Championship
epitaph: Vacant since TTW's own closure, the Television Championship was filled by Felix Sandoval in a ladder match on Showdown; he held it through a controversial time-limit-draw defense against Brandon Franklin before losing it to Franklin at Survival, and Franklin lost it in turn to Windham Brody on UPW's own last served Showdown.
notes: The served ledger (television-title-history.html) also carries an unbroken TTW-era reign chain back to Showdown, May 2011; those reigns are not individually registered, for the same reason given on the World Heavyweight Championship's own row.
